title: Adaptive Headroom Controller for KV-aware Batching and Micro-failover
creator: Marco Chen
description: Add an adaptive headroom controller (AHC) in the runtime scheduler that continuously monitors per-GPU memory headroom, per-tenant KV cache occupancy, and real-time batch admission pressure. The AHC should proactively modulate batching admission, reserve emergency memory tokens, and orchestrate graceful micro-failovers to quantized/trimmed model variants when memory pressure crosses soft thresholds. Goal: reduce production OOMs by >= 90% for mixed-length traffic while keeping P99 latency regression <= 12% and token cost increase <= 6%.
acceptance_criteria: AHC observes GPU-level free memory and KV usage at 250ms cadence and exposes metrics to Prometheus (gpu_memory_headroom_bytes, kv_resident_pct, ahc_actions_total)
Batch admission controller integrates with AHC to dynamically adjust max_batch_size and batch_timeout per-queue based on headroom signals
Memory reservation tokens (MR-tokens) implemented: prioritized requests can acquire low-latency MR-tokens to avoid eviction during critical completion windows
Micro-failover path implemented: when headroom < soft_threshold for >1s, requests are routed to preloaded low-memory model variants (quantized or slim) with preserved API compatibility
System falls back to retry-with-jitter and model fallback chain (primary -> quantized-8 -> slim-128) and records fallback events for SLO audit
End-to-end integration tests simulate progressive KV pressure and verify no OOM crash in 1000 synthetic sessions; empirical P99 latency regression <= 12%
Runbook updated with AHC troubleshooting steps, knobs, and emergency disable toggle
Design doc and prod rollout plan reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads

decisions: Use 250ms sampling cadence as compromise between signal stability and CPU overhead
Prioritize MR-tokens for requests that include response-completion headers (eg. bulk inference jobs) rather than short chat turns
Micro-failover uses prewarmed quantized-8 variants; fallback to slim-128 only after quantized latency > 2x baseline
AHC actions are rate-limited and logged to avoid feedback loops caused by aggressive oscillation

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: AHC oscillation could create latency spikes. Mitigation: implement hysteresis windows and exponential backoff for action frequency.
Risk: Fallback to quantized variants may reduce output fidelity. Mitigation: tag fallback events and correlate with quality evals; enable prompt-level upward routing if degeneration is high.
Risk: MR-token starvation for low-priority tenants. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant token budgets and leak-rate replenishment policy.
Risk: Telemetry overhead at high QPS. Mitigation: adaptive sampling and aggregated metrics with worst-case knobs to reduce cadence to 1s
test_plan: Unit tests for AHC decision logic, hysteresis, and MR-token accounting
Integration tests: CI job that executes 10k mixed-length requests with synthetic KV pressure ramps
Chaos tests: randomized GPU memory spikes and KV eviction events with validation that no worker OOMs
Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 48h with alert thresholds on fallback_rate and p99_latency
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal dev clusters with synthetic load—validate telemetry and invariants
Stage 1: Canary in one region (5% traffic) with SLO monitors and auto-disable on >0.5% error increase
Stage 2: Gradual 25% -> 50% -> 100% if fallback events remain below target and no OOMs observed
Emergency: SRE can toggle ahc.disable via feature flag; automated rollback if p99 increase > 20%
